\paragraph{Reading the map.}
The compliance envelope is not widest at mid-supply. It is pinched to well under
\SI{1}{\micro\ampere} of span below \SI{0.7}{\volt}, widens steadily through the middle
of the range to a maximum of \SI{12.40}{\micro\ampere} of span at
\SI{1.8}{\volt} (\SIrange{-7.04}{5.36}{\micro\ampere}), then collapses again above
\SI{2.0}{\volt}. Closed-loop output resistance follows the same shape inverted, from
\SI{460}{\kilo\ohm} at the bottom of the range down to \SI{5.7}{\kilo\ohm} at
\SI{1.8}{\volt} and back to \SI{336}{\kilo\ohm} at the top: where the output devices are
deep in saturation the loop holds the node stiffly, and where they are not, it cannot.
At the mid-supply point the potentiostat would actually sit on, \SI{1.2}{\volt}, the
usable range is only \SIrange{-1.51}{1.40}{\micro\ampere}.

Below \SI{0.3}{\volt} and above \SI{2.2}{\volt} the zero-load error column already
exceeds \SI{50}{\milli\volt}: the buffer does not track its input at any load, so those
rows describe the external current needed to drag the output onto the commanded value,
not a drive capability. They are shown because the envelope legitimately ceases to exist
there, which is a property of the block worth seeing, not a gap in the data. The
usable-range edges agree with the small-signal figure quoted earlier in this section:
unity-gain tracking holds from about \SI{0.3}{\volt} to about \SI{2.0}{\volt}.

Against the rev-2 target of \(\pm\SI{33}{\micro\ampere}\) into the counter electrode,
the amplifier as biased is roughly twenty times short at the operating point. That is
the headline of this section.

\paragraph{This is one corner, and not the one that matters most.}
The run is the \textbf{ff} corner --- \texttt{cor\_std\_mos.scs} selects
\texttt{section=ff} --- but the imported corner set pins the passive rows at typical in
every corner: \texttt{cor\_res.scs} selects \texttt{tt\_res} and \texttt{cor\_mim.scs}
selects \texttt{tt\_mim}. So the figure is fast transistors with \emph{typical}
resistors, and it should not be read as an extreme of anything.

That distinction is not academic for this block. A1's bias current is set by a poly
resistor in the local bias generator, which makes the resistor corner the dominant
sensitivity: a separate spot check at \SI{1.25}{\volt} gives
\(\pm\SI{1.7}{\micro\ampere}\) for ff transistors with \texttt{tt\_res} against
\(\pm\SI{6.2}{\micro\ampere}\) with \texttt{ff\_res}, on \SI{54.9}{\micro\ampere} of
supply against \SI{85.5}{\micro\ampere}. The resistor corner alone moves the drive by a
factor of \num{3.6} --- more than any transistor corner does. The \SI{54.79}{\micro\ampere}
this run draws at \SI{1.2}{\volt} matches the first of those, which is the check that the
map is the corner it claims to be.

The corner rows should be fixed and the sweep re-run across all five process corners
before any number here is treated as signed off. Until then, read this map as one
sample of the design space --- the shape is trustworthy, the absolute values are not
bounded by it.
